description:
FILED s473t6d (Opus, 2026-09-20) by #1501 round 11 (CHECK 1 on t/op/die.t).

`cl/pcl-test.lisp` exports `pl-isa_ok` (lines 152/162) and implements it
correctly -- it routes through `test-ok`, so the row is NUMBERED and counted,
and it uses Test::More's four-way naming.

`perl-tests/t/test.pl:658` ALSO defines it, in plain Perl, and PCL transpiles
the stub like user code, so the stub's definition WINS:

    sub isa_ok {
        my ($obj, $class, $name) = @_;
        $name //= "object isa $class";
        if (ref($obj) && UNIVERSAL::isa($obj, $class)) {
            print "ok - $name\n";            # <-- no number, no counter
            return 1;
        } else {
            print "not ok - $name\n";
            return 0;
        }
    }

Two lines below it the file's own comment says
`# cmp_ok - provided by pcl-test.lisp, do NOT define here or it will override`.

TWO divergences from perl's `t/test.pl:1656`, which is the ORACLE for both
populations:

  1. NO TEST NUMBER and no counter bump.  perl calls `_ok(!$diag, _where(),
     $name)`.  The stub's bare `print "ok - $name\n"` is parsed by the
     harness as a row it cannot number, so every LATER row in the file is
     numbered one too low and the file's total falls short.
  2. WRONG DESCRIPTION.  perl builds `"$obj_name isa $class"` with
     `$obj_name` defaulting to `'The object'`; the stub uses the caller's
     name ALONE when one is given, and `"object isa $class"` otherwise.  The
     description is a JOIN KEY for the row baselines, so the row can never
     match.

MEASURED, `t/op/die.t`: perl prints
`ok 11 - $@ is an Error object isa Error` and
`ok 13 - returning a different object than what was passed in, via PROPAGATE isa Out`;
PCL prints `ok - $@ is an Error object` and
`ok - returning a different object than what was passed in, via PROPAGATE`,
both unnumbered, and its rows 6..18 carry perl's numbers 14..26.  Both rows
sit in `baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv` as `(missing)`.

BLAST RADIUS (perl 5.40.3 t/, measured): 7 files use `isa_ok`, 24 call
sites -- `t/op/die.t` (3 sites, but 6 rows because five of them are inside a
`$SIG{__DIE__}` handler), `t/class/class.t`, `t/class/utf8.t`,
`t/test_pl/can_isa_ok.t` (7 sites -- test.pl's own test of this very sub),
`t/lib/dbmt_common.pl` (8); plus `perl-tests/die.t` (4) in the sweep
population.

SHAPE: delete the stub's `sub isa_ok` if `pl-isa_ok` can be made to answer
perl's `t/test.pl` naming for this population, or -- more likely, since
`pl-isa_ok` deliberately implements TEST::MORE's naming for the CPAN
population -- keep the stub's sub but build perl's name
(`"$obj_name isa $class"`, `$obj_name` defaulting to `'The object'`) and emit
it through the stub's own numbered printer (`_tap_line`), never a bare
`print`.  Either way, ONE of the two definitions must stop existing as a
silent override.

BAR: a HARNESS change, so the WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN harness row: full sweep +
companion `--all --quick`, baselines edited row by row (the descriptions are
join keys, so every isa_ok row in both baselines moves).
subject: `isa_ok` is defined TWICE and the harness stub's copy SHADOWS the runtime's: it prints an UNNUMBERED row with the wrong description, desynchronising the rest of the file
